posts.title: LocalTC 0.5.0 is out
posts.summary: A copilot beside you, ATC from the real world, traffic around you, an EFB, and a setup that gets you flying sooner.
posts.author: The LocalTC team
posts.body:
LocalTC 0.5.0 is out. It's the biggest version yet: a first officer in the right seat, ATC that works from the real world's ATIS and traffic, an EFB, and a new setup that gets you flying sooner. Here are the highlights; [the changelog](changelog) has every change.

## A copilot beside you
LocalTC's copilot used to live on the radio. Now it sits next to you, on an intercom key of its own. Talk to it like a real first officer:
- **Callouts** in their moment: V1 and rotate from your SimBrief speeds, minimums from the chart, and a heads-up when something's off.
- **Real checklists**, read against the aircraft itself. When an item isn't set it says so, and it never makes up a checklist that isn't there.
- **Its own side of the cockpit**: flaps, gear, lights, the autopilot's settings and the seatbelt sign, when you ask ("flaps three and let's do the approach checklist"). It reads back what it heard before doing anything, and asks when it isn't sure.
- **The radio, if you want**: switch it on and it works ATC with you, from the readbacks to the whole radio.

Pick who it is in the setup guide: each copilot has its own voice and personality. The safety calls are the same whoever you choose.

![On final](img/leg-final.jpg)

## ATC from the real world
- **The real ATIS, worldwide**, read whole: its letter, runways, approaches and closures, and ATC works to them. When the destination changes runways before your approach, you'll hear about it.
- **A runway for each flight**, from the live traffic.
- **Controllers who sound like where they are**, work in shifts, and have personalities of their own.
- **Holds, conditional clearances, terrain-aware vectors** and an arrival sequence with other aircraft in it.

## Traffic around you (experimental)
Turn on **LocalTC's traffic** and the real flights near you taxi, depart and land with you. The ramps fill up with parked aircraft as busy as the airport really is at that hour. It's experimental: tell us what looks wrong.

## The EFB, charts and taxi guidance
An electronic flight bag in the app and on your phone: **ChartFox charts**, the briefing for your airports, **Airport Ops** for your gate and turnaround, and the copilot's checklist. **Taxi guidance** draws the way to the runway or your gate.

## A new setup, and a guide on the first start
**LocalTC-Setup.exe** now carries everything LocalTC needs to start. No console windows, nothing downloaded during the install. When LocalTC opens the first time, its **setup guide** downloads the right models for your PC, installs Ollama (the engine for the language model on your PC) and GPU support if you have an NVIDIA card, sets up your microphone and push-to-talk, and lets you pick your copilot. After that, flights work offline.

## On the dashboard
- **Stats**: equator and date-line crossings, a world map of the countries you've flown to, your airlines and aircraft. It's off until you turn it on in the app.
- **Every Wrapped**: any week, month or year since your first flight.
- **This blog**, which you can **follow** to get new posts by email.

## Getting it
**On 0.4.0?** LocalTC tells you the update is ready (or check now: Settings, then Updates). It never updates mid-flight, and your settings, logbook and models stay.

**New here?** [Download LocalTC-Setup.exe](https://github.com/duckiest428/LocalTC/releases/latest/download/LocalTC-Setup.exe). Windows may warn that the installer is from an unknown publisher (it isn't code-signed yet): choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

## Thank you
Every report sent from the app made this version better. Keep them coming: the gear, then **Support & feedback**, or come and say hello on [the LocalTC Discord](https://discord.gg/fDKfMxfC9a). Next up is 0.5.5.

Happy flying!

posts.title: Welcome to the LocalTC blog
posts.summary: Where the news goes: new versions, what's being worked on, and how it's made.
posts.author: The LocalTC team
posts.body:
LocalTC has grown a lot since its first version: controllers that answer you, a copilot that runs checklists and works the radios, a logbook with replays, Wrapped, and a phone app that follows the flight. The changelog says what changed, version by version. This blog is for the rest: why something changed, what's coming next, and the odd story from the frequency.

## What you'll find here
- **New versions**, with the highlights and a few pictures, when they come out.
- **What's being worked on**, before it's ready, so you can say what you think.
- **How it's made**: how ATC understands a readback, how the copilot decides what to say, and why it all runs on your own PC.

## Your logbook, in numbers
The dashboard has a new **Stats** page: equator and date-line crossings, the countries you've flown to with a passport stamp for each, your airlines and aircraft, the days you flew, and from the sim itself the fuel burned, night landings and the coldest air outside. It's off until you turn it on in the app (Settings, then Account, then **Stats and metrics**), and turning it off again deletes those numbers from your account.

Wrapped now goes back as far as your first flight, too: every week, month and year, with a chart of them all to pick from.

## Say hello
Ideas, questions or a flight that went wrong: write from the [dashboard's Support page](dashboard#support), or [open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/duckiest428/LocalTC/issues). Happy flying.
